title: A Transcriptomic Approach to Elucidate the Mechanisms of Gefitinib-Induced Toxicity in Healthy Human Intestinal Organoids.
authors: Rodrigues, Daniela; Herpers, Bram; Ferreira, Sofia; Jo, Heeseung; Fisher, Ciaran; Coyle, Luke; Chung, Seung-Wook; Kleinjans, Jos C S; Jennen, Danyel G J; de Kok, Theo M
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用转录组学分析吉非替尼在肠道类器官中的毒性机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Gefitinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that selectively inhibits the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), hampering cell growth and proliferation. Due to its action, gefitinib has been used in the treatment of cancers that present abnormally increased expression of EGFR. However, side effects from gefitinib therapy may occur, among which diarrhoea is most common, that can lead to interruption of the planned therapy in the more severe cases. The mechanisms underlying intestinal toxicity induced by gefitinib are not well understood. Therefore, this study aims at providing insight into these mechanisms based on transcriptomic responses induced in vitro. A 3D culture of healthy human colon and small intestine (SI) organoids was exposed to 0.1, 1, 10 and 30 microM of gefitinib, for a maximum of three days. These drug concentrations were selected using physiologically-based pharmacokinetic simulation considering patient dosing regimens. Samples were used for the analysis of viability and caspase 3/7 activation, image-based analysis of structural changes, as well as RNA isolation and sequencing via high-throughput techniques. Differential gene expression analysis showed that gefitinib perturbed signal transduction pathways, apoptosis, cell cycle, FOXO-mediated transcription, p53 signalling pathway, and metabolic pathways. Remarkably, opposite expression patterns of genes associated with metabolism of lipids and cholesterol biosynthesis were observed in colon versus SI organoids in response to gefitinib. These differences in the organoids' responses could be linked to increased activated protein kinase (AMPK) activity in colon, which can influence the sensitivity of the colon to the drug. Therefore, this study sheds light on how gefitinib induces toxicity in intestinal organoids and provides an avenue towards the development of a potential tool for drug screening and development.
abstract_zh: 吉非替尼是一种酪氨酸激酶抑制剂（TKI），选择性抑制表皮生长因子受体（EGFR），从而阻碍细胞生长和增殖。由于其作用机制，吉非替尼已被用于治疗表现为EGFR异常高表达的癌症。然而，吉非替尼治疗可能产生副作用，其中腹泻最为常见，在严重情况下可能导致计划治疗中断。吉非替尼诱导的肠道毒性机制尚不清楚。因此，本研究旨在基于体外诱导的转录组反应，深入探讨这些机制。将健康人结肠和小肠（SI）类器官的3D培养物暴露于0.1、1、10和30微摩尔浓度的吉非替尼，最长持续三天。这些药物浓度通过考虑患者给药方案的生理药代动力学模拟确定。样本用于分析细胞活力和caspase 3/7激活、基于图像的结构变化分析，以及通过高通量技术进行RNA分离和测序。差异基因表达分析显示，吉非替尼扰乱了信号转导通路、细胞凋亡、细胞周期、FOXO介导的转录、p53信号通路和代谢通路。值得注意的是，在结肠与小肠类器官对吉非替尼的反应中，与脂质代谢和胆固醇生物合成相关的基因表现出相反的表达模式。这些类器官反应的差异可能与结肠中激活的蛋白激酶（AMPK）活性增加有关，这可能影响结肠对药物的敏感性。因此，本研究揭示了吉非替尼如何在肠道类器官中诱导毒性，并为开发潜在的药物筛选和开发工具提供了途径。
